b: Once we get through today’s poem, we’ll be two weeks deep into this challenge. So, let’s get at it.

For today’s prompt, write a temporary poem. Some people feel that everything and everyone is temporary in a super long-term view (like thousands or millions of years). And that’s fine. But there are many temporary things in a shorter period of time, including temp jobs, paper plates, rebound relationships, and more. The seasons themselves are temporary until the next one comes along. So, think of what’s temporary and write a poem.
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at a Temporary Poem:

This too shall pass, they say,
whenever something goes wrong,
but shall it? Is it a passing phase,
this pain, this dread, this constant
worry wandering in my head?
They say it shall, but how do they know?
I know all things pass, sure,
and people too, but what does
passing really mean in the end
if everything passes in the end
if everyone passes in the end
and even the end shall pass?
Better to never sit and wait
for passing things to turn great;
instead, take all of life in stride
and live as if you are alive.
